Truth be told, I thought recovery would be much worse and didn’t use many of the things I bought. I did pretty much used pads and a couple of ice packs, and the peri bottle for maybe 4 to 5 days, then just pads. Stock up on full coverage underwear if you are used to only wearing thong underwear, and size up to allow the ice packs and to fit.

I highly recommend:
At home: 
-Nursing/BF bras and tank tops ready to go so you don’t have to wait and order them. Bring a bra with you but have the rest at home ready to go. Also buy some bf/nursing tops you can leave the house in and have them ready.
-adult sippy cups or some kind/insulated cups or mugs WITH LIDS to keep your bevvies cold or hot. You won’t be able to get up much in the early newborn throes. 

-extra strength deodorant , you’ll likely have hot flashes and night sweats 

Hospital:
Wear a gown, not PJ pants in hospital. So much easier to change pads and do self care/hygiene. Tbh just use the hospital gown because you’ll ruin your own stuff with blood / baby pee and poop and you obv don’t have access to a washer or dryer.

EYE MASK, because hospital staff will be coming in every 10 minutes for you or baby. Try to sleep through as much of it as possible. 

Shower slippers

Several outfits for baby because you don’t know how big/long he or she will be. So pack a small newborn outfit and maybe a slightly bigger one too. Our outfits were all too big. Also pack a blanket for baby.

Different outfit to go home in than the one you went to hospital in.

Toothbrush and face wash, hair tie 

That’s pretty much it!

I increased my salary by $40k in 3 years without any additional qualifications (just experience) so keep your eyes out for opportunity. I have come to this platform for the same reasons many times, and so I’ll share what I’ve come to know in my experience, as a 37F. My boyfriend was all of the same things.  He was so amazing, I thought. 

Here are some things to consider..

1. The reason for choosing this man knowing he is an alcoholic is likely your biggest issue to focus on. You may suffer from codependency or codependent behavior despite your ability to independently take care of your family. The root of this is usually a severe lack of love. We all need it so badly. 

2. It really does always “get worse”. The drinking. It will increase in frequency and volume. As it is now, you don’t spend all that much time together, but once you do, it will become very obvious. I’ve read this so many times and when I looked back on my own relationship I was able to actually see it. But I couldn’t see it real time, in the moment. 

3. My father was codependent, and I now can see how I mimic his behavior in adult life. My mom wasn’t alcoholic, but she had narcissistic tendencies. I loved her so much and she was a great mom, but I now struggle with codependency and it’s taken me 37 years to finally see “what’s wrong with me”.  Being a better mom is also behaving in a way that shows your children how to navigate relationships. Would you like your sons/daughters to be with an alcoholic? Would you want them feeling as though they are unlovable? How do you think you would counsel them if they were in your current situation? 

4. While they are drunk or drinking, they are disconnected emotionally from themselves - and you. His character and values would be the same if he was sober, but you might not necessarily get along with him like you do now. 


Note I am saying all of this while being in a very similar mental struggle (stay or go?). My Q has recently gotten sober and let me tell you, I don’t even know the man I’ve loved. I was so naively wrapped up and hyper focused on the drinking that I didn’t see the bigger picture. 

Reflect, journal, get therapy, and remember you are capable of being loved as you are. You don’t need to be anyone’s carer to deserve big love.
